newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra prognosis still "good" after heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra prognosis still "good" after heart attack.

text.p: Entertainer Frank Sinatra remained in hospital on Friday recovering from a heart attack and his prognosis was still good, his spokeswoman Susan Reynolds said.
Sinatra's doctor Rex Kennamer had not changed his prognosis from Thursday, when the singer and Oscar-winning movie actor was admitted to Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, she said.
Kennamer said Sinatra, 81, had suffered "an uncomplicated heart attack."

Reynolds denied a report by NBC news that Sinatra was suffering from degenerative Alzheimer's disease. Local KNBC television also quoted Sinatra's son Frank Jr. as denying his father had the disease that has afflicted former president Ronald Reagan.
Sinatra was rushed to Cedars-Sinai just two days after being released from the same Beverly Hills hospital where he spent Monday night for an undisclosed complaint.
Sinatra's wife Barbara, his children and other relatives were regularly visiting him, Reynolds said.
Sinatra also spent eight days in Cedars-Sinai last November after being admitted for a pinched nerve and later developing pneumonia.
